insights.headline: Gold eases to $3,565 in thin holiday trade as December hike bets harden; silver outshines on MCX
insights.summary: Spot gold eased to $3,565.50 an ounce in thin Thanksgiving trading as traders priced a near-certain Federal Reserve rate hike in December after hot October PCE data, while silver edged up to $41.42. On MCX, gold futures ended near Rs 1,24,559 per 10 g and silver near Rs 1,50,130 per kg after recovering from their lowest levels in over a year. The dollar stayed near a 22-month peak, and Turkey's central bank paused purchases of domestically mined gold.
points: Spot gold was near $3,565.50 an ounce late Thursday, down 0.63%, while silver held near $41.42, up 0.33%, in thin Thanksgiving trading.
MCX February gold ended at Rs 1,24,559 per 10 g, up 0.9%, and March silver at Rs 1,50,130 per kg, up 2.8%, on short-covering.
Fed funds futures price a 99.4% chance of a December rate hike after October core PCE inflation came in at 3.3% and headline PCE at 3.8%.
The dollar index was steady at 103.81, just below a 22-month peak of 104.53 hit on Monday, as AI-stock worries kept markets volatile.
Turkey's central bank suspended purchases of domestically produced gold until further notice; it mines about 30 tonnes a year and holds some 800 tonnes.

brief.headline: Gold slips to $3,565 as Fed hike bets harden
brief.summary: MCX gold ended near Rs 1,24,559 per 10 g as spot gold eased to $3,565.50 on near-certain December Fed hike bets.

bullets.text: MCX gold ended near Rs 1,24,559 per 10 g and silver near Rs 1,50,130 per kg; spot gold was $3,565.50 and silver $41.42 in late US trading.
Kitco reports a 99.4% chance of a December hike after hot October PCE, while a firm dollar near a 22-month peak kept gold under pressure.
Watch: ISM manufacturing PMI on Monday, Dec 1 at 20:30 IST, then US jobs and the RBI policy decision on Dec 4 ahead of the Fed on Dec 9.

trending.title: Fed hike bets pin gold near 14-month lows
trending.summary: Hot October PCE hardened bets on a December hike to near-certainty, and gold eased to $3,565.50 in thin holiday trading after briefly breaking below $3,500.

trending.title: MCX bullion snaps back from one-year lows
trending.summary: Gold and silver futures on MCX recovered on short-covering, with February gold at Rs 1,24,559 per 10 g and March silver at Rs 1,50,130 per kg.

trending.title: Dollar near 22-month peak as AI rout rattles markets
trending.summary: The dollar index held at 103.81, just below a 22-month peak, as doubts about the AI trade kept markets volatile and supported Fed tightening bets.

trending.title: Central banks split on gold
trending.summary: The RBI repatriated another 60 tonnes of gold in 2026, while Turkey's central bank paused purchases of domestically mined gold until further notice.

items.title: Gold slips, silver gains as Fed rate hike expectations persist in holiday trading - Kitco PM Report
items.summary: Spot gold eased in thin Thanksgiving trading as expectations of further Federal Reserve rate hikes and a firm dollar kept buyers cautious, Kitco reports, while silver edged higher. Gold traded near $3,565.50 an ounce, down 0.63%, and silver near $41.42, up 0.33%. Markets price a 99.4% chance of a December hike after hot October PCE data showed core inflation at 3.3%.

items.title: Silver Prices Jump 3% on MCX to ₹1,48,336 per Kg; Kotak Neo Sees Scope for Further Recovery
items.summary: MCX December silver jumped 3.6% to ₹1,48,245 per kg in morning trade, touching an intraday high of ₹1,48,336, as short-covering drove a rebound from Wednesday's low of ₹1,36,712. Kotak Neo said the heavy selling leaves scope for further recovery if silver holds above ₹1,45,400, with ₹1,53,000 the next level in focus. Silver is still nearly 19% below its November 10 close.

items.title: India Bullion: Rise from lowest levels in over a year on short-covering
items.summary: Gold and silver futures on MCX recovered from their lowest levels in over a year on short-covering in thin Thanksgiving trading, Informist reports. The February gold contract ended at Rs 1,24,559 per 10 g, up 0.9%, and March silver at Rs 1,50,130 per kg, up 2.8%, even as a firm dollar and Fed hike expectations capped gains.

items.title: Gold steadies after hitting over 1-year low; Fed outlook in focus
items.summary: Spot gold steadied at $3,580.87 an ounce early Thursday after briefly falling below $3,500 on Wednesday, the first time since September 2025, Reuters reports, as investors covered shorts ahead of Thanksgiving; December futures rose 1.2% to $3,578.70. Silver rose 1% to $41.64. Hot US inflation and GDP revised up to 4.3% reinforced expectations of Fed rate hikes in December and early 2027.

items.title: Dollar lingers near 22-month peak as AI worries simmer
items.summary: The dollar hovered just below a 22-month peak in holiday-thinned trading, Reuters reports, with the dollar index steady at 103.81 after touching 104.53 on Monday. Traders watched AI-linked stocks for direction, and a December Fed hike is seen as a near certainty. A firm dollar keeps pressure on gold.

items.title: Gold, silver prices rebound on MCX, Comex on buying at lower levels
items.summary: MCX December gold traded at ₹1,22,780 per 10 g, up ₹1,643, and silver at ₹1,47,513 per kg, up ₹4,996, as buyers stepped in after the slide to near one-year lows. Comex gold traded near $3,575 an ounce, with the rebound led by short-covering and lower-level buying.

items.title: Gold (XAUUSD), Silver, Platinum Forecasts – Gold Retreats As Traders Rush To Take Profits After Rebound
items.summary: Gold pulled back as traders took profits after Wednesday's rebound, FXEmpire reports, with FedWatch pricing a December hike at 99.4%. Support sits at $3,500–$3,520 and resistance at $3,600. Silver tested $42 as the gold/silver ratio pulled back below 86, with $44.50–$45.00 next if silver holds above $41.

items.title: What is driving fall in gold, silver & crude oil? Fed rate hike fears weigh
items.summary: Gold, silver, crude oil and base metals all slipped as growing bets on further US Federal Reserve rate hikes sapped demand, BusinessLine reports, with markets awaiting US data and the December rate decision.

items.title: PCE Inflation Rises to 3.8% as Stocks, Gold and Silver Weaken
items.summary: US PCE inflation rose 3.8% over the year to October, matching forecasts, while core PCE rose 3.3%, above the 3.2% expected. Both rose 0.3% on the month. Stocks fell after the release and gold and silver hit new lows for the day, with the dollar slightly weaker.

items.title: MCX gold plunges ₹4,420/10g, silver sheds nearly ₹8,800/kg as PCE data fuels December Fed rate hike bets
items.summary: MCX gold fell 3.6% to ₹1,17,906 per 10 g and silver dropped ₹8,800 to ₹1,36,712 per kg on Wednesday evening, Mint reports, as hotter-than-target US inflation strengthened bets on Federal Reserve rate hikes and lifted the dollar.

items.title: India’s central bank repatriates another 60 tonnes of gold in 2026 as share of FX reserves drops to 14.38%
items.summary: The RBI moved 60.08 tonnes of gold from overseas vaults to domestic storage in April–September 2026, Kitco reports, taking the domestic share to 84.05% of its 880.52 tonnes. The remaining 140.39 tonnes stay with the Bank of England and the BIS. Gold's share of forex reserves fell to 14.38% from 16.70% in March as total reserves rose to $737.78 billion.

items.title: Turkish central bank suspends its purchases of domestically produced gold, bankers say
items.summary: Turkey's central bank has suspended purchases of domestically produced gold until further notice, bankers told Reuters, without giving a reason. Turkey mines about 30 tonnes a year and the bank holds around 800 tonnes. The pause breaks a run of central-bank buying that has long supported gold.

items.title: Gold Makes 17% Loss from Last Thanksgiving, Worst Since 2013
items.summary: Gold and silver held on to Wednesday's steep rebound from 15-month lows in thin Thanksgiving trading, BullionVault reports, with gold flat near $3,606 and silver around $41.50. Gold has lost 16.6% over 12 months, its worst such fall since the 28% crash of 2013, while silver is down 22.2% on the year. Fed funds futures price a 99.5% chance of a December hike.

items.title: Gold demand remains strong despite price correction, says World Gold Council
items.summary: India's physical gold demand remains firm despite the correction, the World Gold Council's Sachin Jain said, with consumers buying on dips and ETF inflows recovering in the first half of November. Central banks bought more than 345 tonnes in the previous quarter, and gold ETF holdings were about 126 tonnes at end-October.

items.title: Gold loan growth slows as falling gold prices push lenders into collection mode
items.summary: Gold-loan companies are shifting from growth to collections after the sharp fall in bullion pushed loan-to-value ratios higher, with portfolio LTVs at some NBFCs crossing 75% and certain segments breaching 85%. Lenders are asking borrowers to repay part of their loans or pledge more gold, and analysts expect stress to show in asset quality from the December quarter.

Silver traded 0.5% higher near $41.30 in European trading, recovering after hitting a fresh almost 15-month low of $38.20 the previous day, as US Treasury yields eased to a fresh two-month low near 4.80% and traders slightly trimmed bets on a larger January Fed hike. FXStreet notes rallies remain vulnerable while silver holds below its 20-day average near $46.99.
items.title: Silver Price Forecast: XAG/USD holds ground amid setback in US bond yields
Rupee falls 20 paise to 92.40 against US dollar in early trade
items.summary: The rupee eased 20 paise to 92.40 against the dollar in early trade on Thursday, Economic Times reports, pulling back after hitting an eight-month high of 92.1850 in the previous session. A softer rupee raises the landed cost of gold imports even as global prices steady.

items.title: India Bullion: Fall to lowest in over a year; US tariff proposal weighs
items.summary: Gold and silver futures on MCX and COMEX fell further, Informist Media reports, as a stronger dollar and rate-hike bets weighed after US inflation data matched forecasts. MCX December gold closed down 1.6% at Rs 1,20,429 per 10 g and silver down 3.2% at Rs 1,40,797 per kg, while COMEX silver touched a near-15-month low of $39.56. A US tariff plan for 14 economies, including India, also weighed.

items.title: A big shift for gold trading? JPMorgan, HSBC and StoneX complete first digital gold deals- What to know
items.summary: JPMorgan, HSBC and StoneX completed London's first live trades under the World Gold Council's Wholesale Digital Gold initiative, Mint reports, using fractional ownership in standard 400-ounce bars as collateral without moving the metal. ICE Benchmark Administration ran the pilot with technology from Baton Systems, and the system is meant to work alongside the existing over-the-counter market.

items.title: Gold price tracker, Nov 26: MCX gold rally reclaims ₹1.23 lakh, silver rates surge by ₹5,281/kg; further recovery ahead?
items.summary: MCX gold rallied 1.6% to an intraday high of ₹1,23,074 per 10 g in early trade on Thursday, while silver surged ₹5,281 per kg to ₹1,47,798, Upstox reports, as bullion tracked the global rebound on steady Treasury yields and value buying. At the 9 am open, gold was up ₹1,409 at ₹1,22,546 per 10 g and silver up ₹4,317 per kg.
